## Circular to Licensed Corporations and Associated Entities

## Anti-Money Laundering / Combating Terrorist Financing Non-cooperative Countries and Territories ('NCCTs')

The Financial Action Task Force on Money Laundering ('FATF') regularly updates its list of NCCTs.  At its recent plenary meeting, it has decided to remove Guatemala from the list of NCCTs.  The updated list of the remaining 6 NCCTs is as follows:

| Cook Islands   | Indonesia   | Myanmar     |
|----------------|-------------|-------------|
| Nauru          | Nigeria     | Philippines |

Licensed  corporations  and  associated  entities  are  reminded  to  give  special  attention  to businesses and transactions with persons, including companies and financial institutions, in the  above  NCCTs,  in  accordance  with  Recommendation  21 Note  1 of  the  FATF  Forty Recommendations.

The FATF will regularly review the NCCT list.  Changes to the list, if any, will be conveyed to  licensed  corporations  and  associated  entities  through  circulars  in  due  course.    Further information on the FATF work in respect of NCCTs is also available on the website of FATF at www.fatf-gafi.org.

If there is any question regarding the content of this circular, please contact Ms Madonna Yip at 2842-7618.

## Intermediaries &amp; Investment Products Securities and Futures Commission

Note  1 Recommendation  21:  Financial  institutions  should  give  special  attention  to  business  relationships  and transactions  with  persons,  including  companies  and  financial  institutions,  from  countries  which  do  not  or insufficiently  apply  the  FATF  Forty  Recommendations.      Whenever  these  transactions  have  no  apparent economic or visible lawful purpose, their background and purpose should, as far as possible, be examined, the findings established in writing, and be available to help competent authorities.  Where such a country continues not to apply or insufficiently applies the FATF Recommendations, countries should be able to apply appropriate countermeasures.
